impacted.role: declares DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on categories, sources, source_categories, content (fetched_at, created_at, updated_at) and embeddings, plus three updated_at triggers that write CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
init_db applies schema.sql with IF NOT EXISTS and nothing else; get_db_connection opens WAL with check_same_thread=False; there is no schema version and no upgrade step

writes CURRENT_TIMESTAMP itself at 16 sites: the content INSERT's created_at/updated_at, the sources INSERT, every updated_at UPDATE, last_fetched_at, embeddings.created_at and archived_at; fetched_at and published_at are already bound as tz-aware ISO strings
_rfc3339 appends Z to naive datetimes so the API wire format stays RFC3339
reads sqlite directly and parses published_at and last_fetched_at with time.RFC3339 only; a naive or space-separated value fails the parse and is silently dropped
prismis-daemon verify, the post-deploy check that could assert zero naive rows
states the RFC3339 wire contract and documents the _rfc3339 Z-append as the mechanism

constraints.text: Every datetime field in API JSON responses MUST serialize as RFC3339 with an explicit offset; no naive timestamps on the wire. Consumers parse with time.RFC3339 (Go) or datetime.fromisoformat (Python).

Interfaces, schemas and stored data change additively; a breaking change ships with its migration or backfill in the same change. Anything that overwrites or migrates reads its target first and leaves a way back.
SQLite's ALTER TABLE cannot change a column's DEFAULT; changing an existing table's default means rebuilding the table. Triggers can be dropped and recreated freely.

content.created_at and updated_at (line 63), fetched_at (55), sources.created_at/updated_at (29-30), categories (15-16), source_categories.created_at (37) and embeddings.created_at (85) all default to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, SQLite's naive 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' UTC string.

update_content_timestamp (and update_sources_timestamp at 98, update_categories_timestamp at 104) set updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on every UPDATE, so even a tz-aware app-side write of updated_at is overwritten naive by the trigger.

init_db reads schema.sql and executes it; every statement is CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, so an existing database keeps its original defaults and triggers whatever schema.sql now says. No PRAGMA user_version, no ALTER, no migration list exists anywhere in daemon/src.

The content INSERT binds created_at and updated_at as CURRENT_TIMESTAMP literals; the sources INSERT does the same (398); UPDATEs write updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP at 547, 620, 962, 993, 1004, 1061, 1071, 1081, 1138, 1165; last_fetched_at at 990; embeddings.created_at at 1596; archived_at at 1973. The schema defaults are therefore rarely the writer; the application is.
fetched_at falls back to datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(), the project's tz-aware convention ('2026-10-02T21:47:23.240383+00:00'); published_at is bound as item.published_at.isoformat().

fetched_at is stored in four historical string shapes (space or T separator, with or without +00:00); range queries wrap both sides in datetime() to compare them (#61). Live on cerebro 2026-10-02: 20025 space/naive, 2153 T/naive, 193 space/aware, 16113 T/aware, 1 space/naive without fraction.
_rfc3339 returns v.isoformat() if v.tzinfo else v.isoformat() + 'Z'; the naive branch is what keeps the wire RFC3339 for CURRENT_TIMESTAMP rows.

The TUI parses published_at with time.Parse(time.RFC3339, ...) and keeps the value only if err == nil; last_fetched_at the same at line 402. A naive space-separated string fails and is dropped without a message, so every source's last_fetched_at (46 of 46 naive on cerebro) and 149 naive published_at rows render as unset today.

Connections open with check_same_thread=False, journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=5000. The live database on cerebro is 700 MiB, SQLite 3.46.1, 38,485 content rows, 46 sources, 0 categories; naive counts: created_at 38485, updated_at 38485, fetched_at 22179, archived_at 11126, published_at 149; sources: created_at, updated_at, last_fetched_at 46 each.

The daemon's main entry never calls init_db; init_db is reached only by running database.py directly or by verify_chain (verify). There is no place today where the running daemon upgrades its own database.

Because the application writes CURRENT_TIMESTAMP itself at 16 sites and the triggers overwrite updated_at, changing schema.sql's defaults alone (the issue's step 1) would leave every new row naive; the producer-side fix is the 16 write sites plus the three triggers, with the defaults changed for fresh databases.

Replacing the triggers and running the backfill on an existing database needs a versioned, idempotent upgrade step the daemon runs itself before serving (PRAGMA user_version), because no mechanism exists and an operator-run script is recall-dependent; rebuilding tables to change DEFAULTs is unnecessary once no write relies on the default, so the 700 MiB database is never copied.

Backfilling to the RFC3339 'T...+00:00' shape fixes a live display defect in the TUI for free (last_fetched_at never parses today); the TUI needs no code change, and the storage.py datetime() wrappers stay correct for the single remaining shape.

related.query: gh issue list --state open --search "datetime OR timestamp OR timezone OR rfc3339 OR schema OR migration" --json number,title

reuse.what: datetime.now(UTC).isoformat() at line 284 is the one tz-aware timestamp source every write site should bind, in place of the CURRENT_TIMESTAMP literal
init_db / get_db_connection is where a PRAGMA user_version-guarded upgrade (drop and recreate the three triggers, run the backfill) belongs, so the daemon upgrades its own database before serving
prismis-daemon verify is the existing post-deploy check; a zero-naive-rows assertion makes INV-STORAGE-TS-1 a standing guard rather than a one-time query
the datetime() wrappers at 826, 878, 939 already normalise mixed shapes in range queries and keep working after the backfill

open: The issue's fix shape lists schema defaults and the trigger as the producers, but storage.py writes CURRENT_TIMESTAMP itself at 16 sites and the triggers overwrite app-side updated_at: the design must cover those sites, and schema.sql's defaults only matter for fresh databases.
